HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Low angle from the waterline at golden hour. Foreground: blurred spray. Midground: King Suro (LEFT face) waist-deep in bright shallows, coat off, bare wet muscular back and shoulders to the camera, a heavy dark lacquered chest hoisted on one shoulder, seawater sheeting off him. Background, above him at the rail of the red-and-gold ship: Heo Hwangok (SECOND face), deep warm brown skin, fitted violet-purple jeogori, leaning on the rail, blushing, biting her lip, unable to look away. Heo's ship is exactly the attached ship_ayuta board: ornate red-and-gold lacquered hull with painted panels, one great crimson battened sail and a small red mizzen. Ignore the board's bright daylight; repaint it in the scene light. Three planes: dark out-of-focus foreground near the lens, the beat sharp in the midground, the background dissolving into sea haze; more than half the frame quiet negative space. CHARACTER SHEET, left to right: LEFT face = suro, SECOND face = heohwangok; the tile after the faces is an object reference (copy their exact shape). Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. KING SURO — Look: His portrait face: young, warm, a thin moustache and goatee, black hair under a little gold crown. Dress: Purple silk robe with gold-ochre collar bands and sash, as on his portrait. Crown: Gaya gold crown: a gold band with tall upright grass-leaf finials and hanging jade gogok. Colour #e0a33c. QUEEN HU — Look: South Indian princess from Ayuta: deep warm brown skin, clearly darker than every Gaya and Samhan face around her; large dark kohl-lined eyes, full lips, straight nose, blue-black hair coiled low with the purple-tiger binyeo, small gold hoop earrings. Dress: Her portrait silk: violet-purple jeogori with magenta-gold patterned sleeves and cream cuffs, deep violet chima, pale gold sash with tassels. Cut close and tailored: the jacket fitted to the bust and waist, the sash cinched high, the skirt falling clean from the hips; elegant and expensive, never loose, never a sari dump, never pink. Colour #d98fa8. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.
